skill.name: session-watchdog
skill.description: Review recent Claude sessions, classify stalled work, send targeted wake messages, and report blockers using local wake logs and heartbeat checks.
skill.summary: Monitor other Claude sessions and request continuation of stalled tasks with logged wake limits.
skill.author: rabbitdesigns22

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are Markdown delimiters, documented permission settings, or expected local logging rather than malicious behavior. The time command executes an unaudited sibling skill, and separate quota checks and recording permit concurrent wake limits to be exceeded. No evidence found of credential theft, network exfiltration, or instructions to override this audit.

remediation.issue: The time command delegates execution to another installed skill outside this reviewed package.
remediation.suggestion: Use the existing standard-library clock fallback directly, or require explicit approval and integrity verification before executing the external helper.

remediation.issue: Wake eligibility checks and recording are separate, allowing concurrent watchdog runs to exceed quotas.
remediation.suggestion: Reserve wake quota atomically under a file lock before sending messages; finalize delivery records and enforce the five-wake run limit in code.

content.user_title: Monitor Stalled Claude Sessions and Resume Pending Work
content.value_statement: Idle agent sessions can conceal unfinished tasks and unresolved blockers. Session Watchdog reviews recent session activity, requests targeted continuation, and records wake history and heartbeat status.
actual_capabilities: Guide inspection of up to 40 sessions and six recent events per candidate using Claude desktop session tools.
Classify candidates as done, waiting on the user, waiting on background work, stopped mid-task, error, or hung.
Compose targeted wake messages that quote a session's pending step and ask it not to repeat completed work.
Record local wake history and check three-hour spacing and two-wake daily quotas for each session.
Write setup and heartbeat timestamps and print overdue notices using a configurable age threshold.
List today's wake records and provide local time, optionally through another installed time helper.
limitations: Session inspection and messaging require compatible Claude desktop tools; Python alone does not provide these integrations.
Scheduling and prompt-hook installation require separate setup; this package does not install or run a scheduler.
Classification uses limited recent transcript context and cannot reliably determine every task's actual completion state.
Wake quotas lack atomic enforcement across concurrent runs, and the time command can execute an unreviewed external helper.

use_cases.title: Recover Interrupted Development Tasks
use_cases.description: Review recent coding sessions and request continuation when a task stopped after an error or an unfinished promised step.
use_cases.target_user: Developers coordinating multiple Claude coding sessions

use_cases.title: Identify Blocked Background Work
use_cases.description: Distinguish sessions waiting for background tasks from sessions needing a login, approval, or other user input.

use_cases.title: Check Scheduled Monitoring Health
use_cases.description: Use heartbeat and setup timestamps to detect overdue watchdog runs after the application closes or a scheduled run stalls.
use_cases.target_user: Automation operators maintaining scheduled Claude workflows

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Sessions Without Waking
prompt_templates.prompt: Review recent sessions with session-watchdog. Do not send wake messages. Report sessions that appear stalled and identify anything requiring my input.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: review classifications before enabling recovery

prompt_templates.title: Wake Eligible Stalled Sessions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review sessions active within 24 hours. Check wake history before messaging. Wake at most five eligible sessions and leave completed or user-blocked sessions untouched.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: recover stalled tasks with existing tool permissions

prompt_templates.title: Review Wake History and Heartbeat
prompt_templates.prompt: List today's wake records and check whether the heartbeat is over five hours old. Do not wake sessions or change scheduling.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: diagnose recovery activity and monitoring health

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Scheduled Watchdog
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect scheduler support and exact tool permissions. Propose a two-hour watchdog schedule and heartbeat checks. Wait for approval before changing settings or sending messages.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: prepare unattended monitoring with explicit approval

best_practices: Review a classification-only run before enabling messaging, scheduling, or prompt hooks.
Use narrowly scoped permissions and review the optional external time helper before permitting its execution.
Keep one watchdog run active at a time, check wake history, and verify each scheduled run leaves a heartbeat.
anti_patterns: Treating every idle session as unfinished or waking sessions that require user approval.
Running overlapping watchdogs and assuming separate quota checks guarantee hard wake limits.
Granting broad shell permissions or trusting scheduler success labels without checking the final result and heartbeat.

faq.question: Does this skill start its own scheduler?
faq.answer: No. It provides scheduling guidance and heartbeat commands. You must configure scheduling and any prompt hook separately.

faq.question: Can I use it with Codex alone?
faq.answer: The local helper uses Python, but session inspection and messaging depend on Claude desktop tools not supplied by this package.

faq.question: Which sessions should remain untouched?
faq.answer: Guidance excludes completed, archived, hung, user-blocked, and recently active sessions, plus the current watchdog session.

faq.question: Where does it store monitoring data?
faq.answer: Wake records and heartbeat files are stored locally under ~/.claude/session-watchdog. Wake records include session identifiers, titles, states, and timestamps.

faq.question: Are the wake limits guaranteed?
faq.answer: No. The helper checks spacing and daily counts, but separate checking and recording can race. The five-wake run limit depends on agent compliance.

faq.question: What happens when a heartbeat becomes overdue?
faq.answer: The check-beat command prints a notice after its threshold, normally five hours. It does not restart the scheduler or recover hung sessions.
